tools.name: copy
tools.description: Copy an anchored block verbatim, within or across files.
guidelines: copy/move: move takes copy's fields. To append to a file, anchor its last line with direction after, not a marker line or the block's own end. Only the source's boundary rows and the destination line need reading.
paramDescriptions: 5-char anchor of the FIRST source line.
5-char anchor of the LAST source line.
5-char anchor of the destination line; the block lands before or after it and it may live in another file.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search files with ripgrep; hits are N:│ anchor│content rows (N-│ context), editable without a read.
guidelines: grep: set literal: true when the pattern contains regex metacharacters. A match shown as a ... fragment has an anchor covering the whole line.

tools.name: insert
tools.description: Insert new lines before or after an anchor.
guidelines: insert: check the diff for a missing or extra blank row at block edges.
paramDescriptions: The exact text to insert; an empty string inserts one blank line. Never include the anchor line.

tools.name: move
tools.description: Move an anchored block verbatim, within or across files.

tools.name: outline
tools.description:
Return the symbols of a file, a directory, or a glob such as `src/**/*.ts`: one `anchor│content` row per symbol, where the content is the real first line of that symbol's declaration. Use it before reading a large or unfamiliar file or module, then read only the spans you need.

Each file starts with a `=== path (language) — N lines ===` header. A `[limit N]` line under a row is that symbol's span: `read` with `offset` set to the row's anchor and `limit` set to N returns exactly that symbol. A `[N nested]` line marks children hidden by `depth`. Output stops at 400 rows, and the footer says how to continue. A directory or glob covers supported files only, skips ignored folders, and gives each file a share of the rows; `*` and `**` both cross folders. Files over 200KB are skipped, and a batch stops once it has read 400,000 source lines to protect the session's anchors.

Supported languages: JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX/TSX, Python, Go, Rust, Solidity, Java, PHP, Blade, SCSS, Sass, and Markdown. Any other file, or a file with no symbols, comes back as a head-and-tail preview with a note that says so; an empty file keeps only its empty-file note. A note also says when the parser could not read part of a file, since symbols there may be missing.

A row is only the declaration line: read a symbol's span before you edit inside it. Rows cover top-level declarations and the members of a type or module; a declaration inside a function body is never a row, whatever `depth` you pass. Annotations, decorators, and attributes above a declaration are not shown and are outside its span. A row clipped with a trailing `...` is not served for editing, so read that line first.
tools.snippet: Map the symbols of a file or folder before reading it: one anchored row per declaration, with the span to read
guidelines: `outline`: before you `read` a large or unfamiliar file or module, outline it and read only the spans you need.
`outline`: a span starts at the declaration line; read the lines above it before you delete or move a symbol, so its decorators go with it.
paramDescriptions: File, directory, or glob (e.g. src/**/*.ts) to outline, relative to the working directory; files may also use absolute paths.
Nesting depth to show: 0 lists top-level symbols only, 1 adds their members (default 2, maximum 10).

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a file as anchor│content rows (4-char anchors); supports paging and images.
guidelines: read: after an edit, + and space diff rows carry live anchors and - rows are dead; read again only for anchors you lack.
Remember to use the hashline tools for every file read and edit: `read`, `replace`, `replace_match`, `insert`, `copy`, `move`, or `undo_last_change`.

tools.name: replace
tools.description: Replace whole anchored lines. For part of a line, use replace_match.
guidelines: replace: one line uses the same anchor twice. A pure deletion checks only the boundary lines and removes the interior as it stands.

edit tools: text is the exact content without anchor prefixes; escapes are decoded once, so \uXXXX is the character and \\uXXXX stays literal. A trailing line break sets the newline of the last line written instead of adding a blank line; a lone newline writes one blank line.
edit tools: same-file calls in one message form one batch; one undo reverts all.
paramDescriptions: 5-char anchor of the FIRST line to remove.
5-char anchor of the LAST line to remove.
The exact text to write in place of the removed range. "" deletes the range.

tools.name: replace_match
tools.description: Replace exact fragments within anchored lines.
guidelines: replace_match: old_string is only the fragment that changes; every match in the range changes, so scope the range to the lines that should change. If old_string covers the line except indentation and trailing punctuation, use replace.
paramDescriptions: 5-char anchor of the FIRST line of the range searched.
5-char anchor of the LAST line of the range searched; same as `replace_from` for a single line.

tools.name: undo_last_change
tools.description: Undo a file's latest hashline edit.
guidelines: undo_last_change: one slot per file; undo before any other edit or write to that file.
undo_last_change: undo a cross-file move on both files; undoing one side leaves lines duplicated or missing.
